title: AMZN: Long. Hold 1 sh into the Oct 29 print and add toward ~11 sh after it. Target $280.84 (+12.2%), research target (12m) $278.28 on 23x driver-built EPS plus an AWS-led sum of parts
call_reason: The published target ($280.84) and research target (12m) ($278.28) are both above the $250.38 close, and P(gain) is 0.6279. The edge is modest: the supervisor's confidence is low (its ladder is not used), and conviction scales the expected return from 18.3% to 17.5% (multiplier 0.72).
one_liner: AWS is adding capacity faster than ever: AWS net PP&E reached $263.8B at mid-2026 against a ~$496B backlog. Our driver build turns that into AWS sales of $234.6B in 2027 (+35%) and lets ads carry retail profits. The Anthropic and OpenAI stakes add ~$21/share, which the street's EPS does not count. We price 23x on NTM EPS of $11.32, 13% below consensus; the gap is EBITDA, not D&A (2028: $297.9B vs consensus $355.3B), so the $278.28 research target (12m) and $280.84 target are not stretch numbers; we hold 1 sh and stage the add after the Oct 29 print.

thesis.point: AWS growth is capacity-led and largely pre-sold, so revenue follows the capex.
thesis.evidence: Q2-26 AWS sales were $42.2B (+37%) with $16.6B OI. The backlog is ~$496B with a 6.4-year weighted life, and management says power capacity doubles by end-2027 vs 2025 and 2027 capacity is largely reserved. The driver build rolls AWS net PP&E from $150.4B (FY25 average) to $266.2B / $426.3B / $590.8B averages in 2026-28. Capacity turnover falls from 0.86x to 0.65x / 0.55x / 0.50x. That gives AWS sales of $173.8B / $234.6B / $293.7B, which is +35.0% in 2027 and +25.2% in 2028 (derived: 234.6 / 173.8 - 1; 293.7 / 234.6 - 1). AWS EBITDA margin goes from 57.1% in H1-26 (ex the ~$0.6B energy gain) to 58.5% / 60.0%. The external backdrop is supportive: the cloud market grew +43% y/y in Q2 with Amazon at 28% share, and AWS raised Capacity Block GPU prices ~15% on Oct 7 (P6-B300 now $16.146 per accelerator-hour; the prior $14.04 is from the research).

thesis.point: Ads, not the stores, carry North America + International profit, and that profit compounds even with flat retail margins.
thesis.evidence: Advertising was $68.6B in FY25 and grew +25.1% in H1-26 (Q2 +26.2%). The driver path is $85.4B / $102.5B / $121.0B for 2026-28 (+24% / +20% / +18%). At an assumed 50% ads margin, which is our estimate and not disclosed, stores run at ~0.16% margin held flat. Segment OI still rises from $43.7B in 2026 to $52.3B in 2027 and $61.6B in 2028 (engine rows). The SOTP values this at 22x NTM after-tax OI of $46.9B = $1,032B.

thesis.point: The AI-lab stakes are real equity value that consensus EPS excludes. We count them once, after tax, lock-up and an overlay.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q carries Anthropic at $190.4B, and Amazon committed $50B to OpenAI's Series C. We value Anthropic at a $1.5T IPO, which is 17.60% after the Public Benefit Fund and primary dilution, less 24% tax and a 10.37% lock-up discount, for $183.7B. OpenAI is at cost, $50.0B. Together that is ~$21.19/share on 11.03B horizon shares (derived: (183.7 + 50.0) / 11.03). After the Leo and Zoox loss add-backs (+$72.7B) and their own scenario values (+$22.0B), other investments (+$4.6B), Globalstar (-$10.9B), probability-weighted legal (-$34.5B) and a 10% conglomerate overlay (-$26.0B), the net equity-level items are +$23.72/share (derived: $261.6B / 11.03B) on both legs. The stakes cut both ways: an Anthropic IPO at ~$1.0T takes ~$6.95/share off, and ~$1.92T adds ~$5.53.

variant_view: We sit below the street and slightly above the options market. StockAnalysis shows a median target of $329.50 (average $331.46, Strong Buy); our recency-weighted median of 56 individual analyst targets is $326.23, +30.3% from $250.38. Our $280.84 target is 13.9% below it (derived: 280.84 / 326.23 - 1), and analysts get zero weight in the published target (ex-analyst target $276.13). The gap is earnings, not the multiple. Our driver-built NTM EPS at the Oct-2027 horizon is $11.32, against ~$13.03 on consensus (derived: 0.237 x $10.51 + 0.763 x $13.81), so we are 13.1% below. Driver-built 2028 EBIT is $155.1B vs MarketScreener's $182.7B (-15.1%). The difference is not D&A. We depreciate AWS PP&E at 14% a year on a capex roll that uses consensus 2027-28 capex ($277.4B / $296.9B), yet the build's 2028 D&A of $142.7B is below the $172.6B implied by consensus EBITDA less EBIT (derived: 355.3 - 182.7). The gap is EBITDA: $297.9B vs $355.3B in 2028 (-16.2%, derived), with the stores margin held at ~0.16% (H1-26 0.76%) and ads at an assumed 50% margin. The street's ~$326 implies ~31x FY27 EPS (derived: 326.23 / 10.51 = 31.0x), against a 23.5x CY2027 peer median. Against the options market, the market-only median is $265.01 with P(gain) 0.5615. Our published $280.84 is 6.0% higher (derived: 280.84 / 265.01 - 1) and our P(gain) of 0.6279 is 6.6 points higher. The gap comes from the research leg (weight 0.33, with its calibration shift), whose value includes the ~$21/share of AI-lab stakes. This is a real but small variant: a below-consensus earnings path, with sum-of-parts value the street's P/E does not capture.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $278.28 is the model engine's base horizon value (2027-10-06) on the driver-led set: 0.5 x P/E leg + 0.5 x SOTP leg. P/E leg $284.09: 23x (a 2.3% discount to the 23.5x CY2027 11-peer median; cloud subgroup 22.5x) x driver-built NTM EPS $11.32 = $260.36, plus $23.72/share of equity-level items. SOTP leg $272.47: AWS NTM after-tax OI $70.9B x 25 = $1,772.5B, plus North America + International $46.9B x 22 = $1,032.0B, less a $3.2B venture basis correction = EV $2,801.4B. From that we deduct horizon net debt of $58.4B (incl. finance leases) and add the same equity items, over 11.03B horizon shares (0.9%/yr dilution). The DCF is a diagnostic only, at weight 0 ($182 at a 10.44% WACC with a mid-capex-cycle terminal year). Scenarios are bear $183.10 (p 0.25: AWS turnover -8%, EBITDA margin -2 pts, ads -4%, 17.5x, Anthropic ~$1.0T), base $278.28 (p 0.5) and bull $343.83 (p 0.25: AWS turnover +6%, +1.5 pts, ads +3%, 25.5x, Anthropic ~$1.92T). The model median is $270.60. The driver gate (2026-10-22) moved the research target (12m) $277.36 -> $278.28 by fixing the EPS/EBIT ratio. The three agents' research targets (12m) were $290 / $278 / $267. The $280.84 target is the median of the published 12-month distribution, which weights the options market 0.67 and research 0.33 with a calibration shift (expected value $296.27). Upside from $250.38 is +12.17% to target and +11.14% to the research target (12m) (derived: 280.84 / 250.38 - 1; 278.28 / 250.38 - 1).

catalysts.why_it_moves: The Fed raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% effective Sep 17. The 10-year was 5.31% on Oct 5 and 5.13% on Oct 21 (FRED). AMZN's beta is 1.36, and its value is rate-sensitive through the multiple (the DCF diagnostic swings ~$50/share per point of WACC).
catalysts.watch: A second hike or hawkish guidance that lifts the 10-year back above ~5.3%. It lands the day before the Q3 print, so the two moves compound.

catalysts.event: Microsoft FQ1 FY2027 results, after the close (Azure growth and capex read-across)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the first hyperscaler print of the week. Azure growth and Microsoft's capex framing set the bar for AWS growth and for how the market prices AI capex the next day.
catalysts.watch: Azure growth vs the +43% cloud market, capacity-constraint language, and FY27 capex. Alphabet's Q3 is expected the same week, but its date is not confirmed (estimated late Oct).

catalysts.event: Amazon Q3 2026 results, after the close; call 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the first test of the driver path. Recent print reactions have been large: +15.3% after Q2-26, -5.6% after Q4-25 and +0.8% after Q1-26 (close to close). The bar is the guide of $197-202B sales and $22.5-26.5B OI, against Oct 6 consensus of $202.03B and EPS $1.95.
catalysts.watch: AWS growth vs +37% in Q2 (our 2026 path of $173.8B needs H2 at ~+37%) and AWS margin vs 57%. Also ads growth vs +26%, the Q4 guide, first 2027 capex framing vs $277.4B consensus, any backlog (RPO) change vs ~$496B, and the Anthropic mark in GAAP EPS.

catalysts.event: Black Friday to Cyber Monday (holiday-season read)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Adobe projects US online holiday sales of $275.1B (+6.7%). Third-party spending reads move retail sentiment, but retail is a small part of the value: stores margin is ~0.2% in the build.
catalysts.watch: Adobe/Salesforce online-spend prints vs +6.7%, and any Amazon unit-volume commentary.

catalysts.why_it_moves: The Trainium and agent roadmap, plus Anthropic and OpenAI capacity updates, bear on the AWS EBITDA-margin driver (Trainium mix) and on backlog quality.
catalysts.watch: Trainium generation and pricing, new multi-year AI-lab commitments, and Capacity Block pricing after the ~15% Oct 7 rise.

catalysts.why_it_moves: The same rate channel as October, at a 1.36 beta.
catalysts.watch: The dot plot and the 10-year vs 5.1-5.3%.

catalysts.event: Anthropic public S-1 and IPO pricing (a confidential draft S-1 has been with the SEC since June 2026; we found no public filing)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The stake carries $183.7B in our build at a $1.5T IPO. Pricing at ~$1.0T takes ~$6.95/share off, and ~$1.92T adds ~$5.53. The IPO also re-marks GAAP EPS.
catalysts.watch: A public S-1, which must be on file at least 15 days before a roadshow. Watch the price range vs $1.5T, Amazon's disclosed ownership (we use 19.5% pre-IPO) and lock-up terms.

catalysts.event: California AG antitrust (price-fixing) trial, San Francisco Superior Court
catalysts.why_it_moves: Together with consumer class actions it is a -$4.0B item in the probability-weighted legal deduction. An adverse verdict or injunction would also be read across to the FTC case. The California AG's Apr 16, 2026 release says trial is set for January 19, 2027; we did not check the court docket. One research agent cited a move to Mar 22, 2027, which we could not verify.
catalysts.watch: Any continuance, settlement or injunction on vendor pricing communications.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results and the 2027 capex guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: Last year's capex guide (~$200B) sent the stock -9% after hours and -5.6% close to close. Our build already uses $277.4B of 2027 capex, so the reaction turns on capex vs AWS acceleration.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex vs $277.4B (above ~$300B without AWS acceleration is the bear path), AWS exit growth, and the holiday-quarter ads print.

catalysts.event: FTC v. Amazon monopolization trial begins, W.D. Wash.. Press reports (the docket was not checked): on Oct 9 the judge denied Amazon's request to move it to June 2027.
catalysts.why_it_moves: It is the largest legal item: p(liability) 0.35 on a 3-10% remedy hit to the retail + ads value, -$15.9B in the build. Liability is tried first and remedies later, so a remedy ruling inside the horizon is unlikely. Headlines can still move the stock.
catalysts.watch: Pretrial rulings, settlement talk, and whether the FTC/22-state ad-surcharge suit (filed Aug 31, 2026) is consolidated or survives a motion to dismiss.

risks.risk: AI-capex digestion: AWS growth slides to the low-to-mid 20s while D&A from the capex roll keeps rising. This is the bear case at $183.10 (AWS turnover -8%, AWS EBITDA margin -2 pts, 17.5x).
risks.signpost: AWS growth below ~30% in Q3 or Q4, AWS EBITDA margin below ~55%, a 2027 capex guide above ~$300B with no AWS acceleration, or GPU rental and Capacity Block prices rolling over.

risks.risk: AI-lab concentration: OpenAI and Anthropic are large parts of the ~$496B backlog and large equity marks. Anthropic also signed multi-gigawatt TPU capacity with Google and Broadcom from 2027.
risks.signpost: Backlog (RPO) flat or down in the 10-Q, a renegotiated lab commitment, Anthropic workloads shifting to TPU, or an Anthropic IPO priced below $1.5T (at ~$1.0T, -$6.95/share).

risks.risk: Multiple de-rating with rates: at ORCL's 17.9x CY2027 P/E on FY27 EPS of $10.51, the stock is worth $188, our thesis break, 24.9% below the close (derived: 188 / 250.38 - 1).
risks.signpost: The 10-year back above 5.3% after a hawkish Oct 28 or Dec 9 FOMC, peer CY2027 P/Es compressing toward the 22.5x cloud subgroup or lower, and a close below the $193.10 stop.

risks.risk: Legal remedies: FTC monopolization, the FTC/22-state ad-surcharge suit and the California AG case. We deduct $34.5B probability-weighted (-$3.12/share, derived: 34.45 / 11.03), but the range runs to -$51.2B.
risks.signpost: Adverse pretrial rulings before the Mar 29, 2027 trial, the ad-surcharge suit surviving dismissal (it is -$14.1B in the build: -$4.0B damages, -$10.1B forward pricing), or an injunction in California.

trade.position: 1 sh held (~$250 at $250.38, 1.1% of the $22,770 book, derived: 250.38 / 22,770.31; bought 2026-10-07 @ $256.48). The Sharpe-optimal target is 11.09 sh (12.2% of the book) under a 15% name cap.
trade.entry: The 2026-10-06 supervisor plan was to keep a $230 limit live through the Q3 print and, if it was unfilled, buy 1 sh after the print unless the print threatened the $188 thesis break. The 1 sh was bought on 2026-10-07 @ $256.48, before the print. Today's review action is hold (trade 0 sh). The decider stages adds after the print: its 'after' date of 2026-10-31 was set before Amazon dated the print, which is Oct 29. On a close at or below $249.36 it adds +10 sh to 11. It holds 15 sh at $232.85-$225.34 with no news check and 17 sh at $200.30 after a news check. Every add must still pass the Sharpe test, and the print must not threaten $188.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below the $193.10 stop (15th percentile, -22.9%; touch probability 0.368) or a sustained trade below the $188 thesis break. Take the full position off at $350.53 (+40.0%; the decider sells the last share there; touch probability 0.436); reward/risk is 1.79. Add per the decider ladder above after the print, if AWS growth holds at or above ~30% and 2027 capex framing is not above ~$300B without AWS acceleration. Do not add if AWS growth falls below ~30%; re-run the research instead.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 (Oct 29) shows AWS growth below ~30% (vs +37% in Q2) together with 2027 capex framed above ~$300B. The driver path, and with it the $278.28 research target (12m), would be too high, so we stop adding and re-run.

A close below the $188 thesis break while FY27 consensus EPS is still being revised up (4 up / 0 down in 30 days at the last check). That would mean the market is pricing a structural break (backlog quality or a margin reset), not noise. We exit.

On the upside: AWS holding 35%+ with margins at or above 60%, or an Anthropic IPO at or above ~$1.92T. Both move us toward the $343.83 bull case, and we would re-test the $350.53 full exit rather than sell into it.
